The really mind bendy thing is that time is really just another dimension of our universe. It is now experimentally provable that time can change in certain circumstances. See for instance the twin paradox. Without getting into relativity, the point is that if you have a pair of twins and one gets on a ship and flies away at relativistic rates and then comes back - he will have aged less than his twin (and everybody else) back on Earth. The time could range from minutes to decades to millennia and beyond. This isn't simply theoretical, it's an aspect that is regularly compensated for in any project that involves rapid rates of movement. For instance our GPS satellites are tweaked to compensate with relativistic time dilation - as this effect is known.

So while we easily understand the fact that we could move straight or backwards forever without reaching an endpoint (as in walking around on a sphere, like the earth) it's infinitely more difficult to grasp the concept of going forward or backward in time forever yet it too is little more than another dimension of our very bizarre universe.
